verdict.rationale: Ghostty's only relevant evidence is a claimed built-in AppleScript dictionary for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts and input events. That could in principle let a script act on many sessions at once, but no bulk or broadcast operation is documented. A hands-on runtime probe found no remote-control or IPC interface through the CLI, which further weakens confidence that an external agent can drive multi-item operations. Missing for 10: any documented bulk/broadcast operation across many tabs, splits or sessions; agent-accessible remote-control API; hands-on corroboration that AppleScript automation works for multi-item actions.
